audit_detail.c_quote: bs->viewanglespeed[i] *= 0.45 * (1 - factor);
audit_detail.rust_quote: bs.viewanglespeed[i] *= 0.45 * (1.0 - factor);
audit_detail.impact: C: `0.45` is an unsuffixed double, so `0.45 * (1 - factor)` and the `*=` are evaluated in f64 then narrowed to the f32 field. Rust infers `0.45` as f32 (operand `(1.0 - factor)` is f32), so the whole RHS and the multiply are f32. `0.45` is inexact in both widths, so the two evaluations differ by up to ~1 ULP across the full range of `factor` (0.001..1.0), not just at a boundary. viewanglespeed accumulates frame-to-frame (`+=` elsewhere) and drives bs.viewangles, which is passed to the EA_View trap as a vec3_t — so the divergence is observable at the ABI seam and can compound over frames. Note downstream ANGLE2SHORT quantization may absorb small deltas in some cases.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Match C's double promotion: `bs.viewanglespeed[i] = (bs.viewanglespeed[i] as f64 * (0.45 * (1.0 - factor) as f64)) as f32;` (the `1 - factor` sub-expression is float in C, only the `0.45 *` and the accumulate promote to double). This mirrors how the same porter already handled 0.25/0.15/0.9/0.0012 in BotAimOffsetGoalAngles/BotAimLeading.

audit_detail.c_quote: bs->enemySeenTime > level.time + (ENEMY_FORGET_MS - (ENEMY_FORGET_MS*0.2))
audit_detail.rust_quote: (*bs).enemySeenTime > lt as f32 + (ENEMY_FORGET_MS as f32 - (ENEMY_FORGET_MS as f32 * 0.2))
audit_detail.impact: C: `ENEMY_FORGET_MS*0.2` (0.2 unsuffixed double) is evaluated in f64, so the whole threshold `level.time + (ENEMY_FORGET_MS - ...)` is f64 and the compare promotes the f32 `enemySeenTime` to f64. Rust computes `ENEMY_FORGET_MS as f32 * 0.2` in f32 (0.2 inferred f32), so the threshold is f32. Because 0.2 is inexact, the f64 product is slightly larger than the f32 one (e.g. ENEMY_FORGET_MS=8000 -> f64 sub yields 6399.9999999999998, f32 yields exactly 6400.0). Since enemySeenTime is always an integer-valued float, the two paths only disagree at the exact tick where enemySeenTime == level.time + 0.8*ENEMY_FORGET_MS (reachable: current time == set-time + 0.2*ENEMY_FORGET_MS), at which the f64 path takes the `>` branch (runs CombatBotAI) and the f32 path does not. Marginal (single-ms boundary) but a genuine width divergence, and inconsistent with the porter's f64 handling of the other unsuffixed-double literals in this file.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Evaluate the threshold in f64 to match C: `((*bs).enemySeenTime as f64) > (lt as f64 + (ENEMY_FORGET_MS as f64 - (ENEMY_FORGET_MS as f64 * 0.2)))`.

audit_detail.c_quote: if ( NPCInfo->stats.aggression < Q_irand( 0, 20 ) && NPC->health < NPC->client->pers.maxHealth*0.75f && !Q_irand( 0, 2 ) )   // C compares in float: health promoted to float, RHS is float
audit_detail.rust_quote: && (*npc).health < ((*client).pers.maxHealth as f32 * 0.75f32) as c_int
audit_detail.impact: C evaluates `health < maxHealth*0.75f` (and `*0.5f` at 4266) as a FLOAT comparison; the Rust port truncates the float RHS to c_int and compares as integers. For the `<` operator this is NOT truncation-safe (unlike the `>` sites at rust 1860/1877 which ARE safe). When maxHealth*factor is non-integer and health == floor(that value), the branch flips. Concrete: a Reborn with maxHealth=50 -> 50*0.75f=37.5 -> Rust truncates to 37; at health==37, C `37<37.5`==true but Rust `37<37`==false, so the Jedi fails to trigger the rage/heal/lead behavior it should. Reachable for any odd maxHealth (0.5 site) or any maxHealth not divisible by 4 (0.75 site). Three sites share this pattern: rust 1906 (heal/protect/absorb/rage in Jedi_CombatDistance), rust 2192 (final rage check), rust 4266 (Boba lead in Jedi_FaceEnemy). Note that Boba_FireDecide (rust 638) does the SAME C comparison correctly as a float compare `(*npc).health as f32 < ... * 0.5f32`, confirming the intended pattern.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Match C by comparing in float, as Boba_FireDecide (rust 638) already does: `(*npc).health as f32 < (*client).pers.maxHealth as f32 * 0.75f32` at rust 1906 and 2192, and `(*npc).health as f32 < (*client).pers.maxHealth as f32 * 0.5f32` at rust 4266. Drop the `as c_int` cast that changes the comparison to integer.

audit_detail.c_quote: shotVel[2] += travelTime * 0.5 * NPC->client->ps.gravity;
audit_detail.rust_quote: shotVel[2] += travelTime * 0.5 * (*client).ps.gravity as f32;
audit_detail.impact: C's `0.5` is a double so `travelTime*0.5*gravity` is computed in f64 and the += rounds once when narrowing to the float shotVel[2]; the Rust version computes wholly in f32, rounding at the `*gravity` multiply and again at the +=. Included only for completeness of the double-promotion audit; probably harmless in practice.

audit_detail.impact: Cmd_CallTeamVote_f: C treats arg2 as a numeric client slot whenever its FIRST up-to-3 characters are all digits (it only scans indices 0..2 and ignores anything after). The Rust port instead requires the ENTIRE string to be <=3 chars AND all-digit. For a team-vote target like `kick 0012` (4 chars, client 12 active) C parses atoi=12 and proceeds to vote-kick client 12, while Rust (len 4 > 3) falls into the name-matching branch, fails to find a netname "0012", and rejects with "is not a valid player on your team". Likewise `kick 1234`/`kick 123x` take different branches and emit different error messages. Observable behavioral divergence on team-vote leader/kick with a >3-char numeric-prefixed argument.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Replicate the C scan: iterate i in 0..3 breaking on a non-digit or end-of-string, then `numeric = i >= 3 || i >= bytes.len()` where bytes = arg2_s.as_bytes(). In the numeric branch use an atoi-equivalent (parse the leading digit run) rather than `parse::<i32>().unwrap_or(-1)` so `123x`-style inputs behave like C's atoi.

audit_detail.impact: G_Say builds the chat-name prefix. Raven's `EC` macro is the byte 0x19 (\x19), distinct from the color escape Q_COLOR_ESCAPE+COLOR_WHITE ("^7"). In SAY_ALL the port DROPS the trailing EC entirely (C emits `netname^7\x19: `, Rust emits `netname^7: `). In SAY_TEAM/SAY_TELL the port renders every EC as `^7` instead of \x19 (C: `\x19(netname^7\x19)\x19: `; Rust: `^7(netname^7)^7: `). The exact byte string passed to trap_SendServerCommand for every say/say_team/tell/gc message differs from the oracle, changing how the client parses/renders the chat name (0x19 is a significant delimiter in client chat handling). Observable at the ABI seam for all chat.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Emit the literal 0x19 byte where Raven uses EC. Define `const EC: char = '\u{19}';` and format SAY_ALL as `format!("{}^7{EC}: ", netname)`, SAY_TEAM as `format!("{EC}({}^7{EC}){EC}: ", netname)`, SAY_TELL as `format!("{EC}[{}^7{EC}]{EC}: ", netname)`, keeping `^7` only for the Q_COLOR_ESCAPE+COLOR_WHITE pair.

audit_detail.impact: Cmd_GameCommand_f: Raven's own off-by-one bound `order > 7` (should be `>=`; gc_orders has 7 entries) is transcribed faithfully, so `order == 7` passes the guard. In C `gc_orders[7]` is an out-of-bounds read of a 7-element array (silent UB, reads adjacent static memory). In Rust `gc_orders[7]` is a bounds-checked index that PANICS. Reachable via a malicious `gc <player> 7`. The port faithfully copied C's buggy comparison but the Rust OOB->panic diverges from C's OOB->read and carries no documented §19 defined-behavior note.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Add a §19 note documenting the defined behavior chosen for C's UB, and tighten to `order as usize >= gc_orders.len()` (return instead of indexing OOB) for a deterministic no-op that cannot panic.

audit_detail.bugclass: 2 (f32 math where C promotes through double libm)
audit_detail.c_quote: ent->NPC->goalRadius = sqrt(ent->r.maxs[0]+ent->r.maxs[0]) + sqrt(targ->r.maxs[0]+targ->r.maxs[0]);
audit_detail.impact: C's `sqrt` is the double libm function; the float sum is promoted to double, sqrt'd in f64, the two results summed in f64, then truncated to the int `goalRadius`. Rust `(f32).sqrt()` computes in f32 throughout. The two roots differ by up to an ULP; because the sum is truncated to c_int, a value landing just under an integer (e.g. 4.9999997 f32 vs 5.0000001 f64) truncates to a different navgoal radius, changing NPC arrival/path decisions. Manifests only at truncation boundaries but is a genuine width divergence.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Compute in f64 to match C: `(((*ent).r.maxs[0] as f64 + (*ent).r.maxs[0] as f64).sqrt() + ((*targ).r.maxs[0] as f64 + (*targ).r.maxs[0] as f64).sqrt()) as c_int`.

audit_detail.bugclass: 2 (f32 math where C promotes through double libm)
audit_detail.c_quote: duration = fabs(offset)/fabs(ent->speed)*1000.0f;
audit_detail.rust_quote: duration = (offset.abs() / (*ent).speed.abs()) * 1000.0;
audit_detail.impact: C promotes both operands through `fabs` (double libm) and does the divide and `*1000.0f` in f64, narrowing to the float `duration` only at assignment. Rust `f32::abs` keeps the whole expression in f32. `duration` then flows into Q3_Lerp2Origin where it is stored as `s.pos.trDuration = duration as c_int` (truncated), so a sub-integer f32/f64 difference can produce a different mover trajectory duration. Width divergence verified at the site; observable only at truncation boundaries.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Match C's double evaluation: `duration = ((offset as f64).abs() / ((*ent).speed as f64).abs() * 1000.0) as f32;`.

audit_detail.c_quote:
ent->parms = (parms_t *)G_Alloc( sizeof(parms_t) );
		memset( ent->parms, 0, sizeof(parms_t) );
audit_detail.impact: C explicitly zeroes the freshly-allocated parms_t. Rust drops the memset. G_Alloc (both C and the ported g_mem.rs) is a bump allocator over a pool that is zeroed only at program/BSS init and is NOT re-zeroed by G_InitMemory (only allocPoint resets). On the first level the pool region is already zero so it is harmless, but across a map restart the pool hands back regions still holding a previous level's parms strings; C's memset clears them, Rust leaves stale bytes. The increment path then does `atof(parm[parmNum])` reading a stale non-empty string instead of "", and untouched sibling parm slots read stale in later Q3_GetFloat/Q3_GetString/Q3_GetVector calls. Real divergence gated on pool reuse.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: After allocating, zero the struct to mirror the C memset, e.g. `core::ptr::write_bytes((*ent).parms as *mut u8, 0, core::mem::size_of::<parms_t>());`.

The existing PORT-NOTE(sscanf) explains the parse mechanism but does not record the uninitialized-tail/UB defined-behavior choice.

audit_detail.c_quote: respawn += crandom() * ent->random;
audit_detail.rust_quote: respawn += ((*ctx.world).bg_state.rng.crandom() * (*ent).random) as c_int;
audit_detail.impact: Truncation-point divergence in Touch_Item. C does `respawn = (int)((float)respawn + delta)` — the float sum is truncated toward zero. audit_detail.c_quote: {NULL}  /* fields[] terminator; BG_ParseField loop: for(f=l_fields; f->name; f++) */
audit_detail.rust_quote: field(c"", 0, fieldtype_t::F_IGNORE), // {NULL} sentinel — name left null below  … const fn field: name: name.as_ptr() as *mut c_char
audit_detail.impact: The FIELDS terminator's name is c"".as_ptr() — a NON-null pointer to an empty string, not NULL. BG_ParseField (bg_misc.rs) ends its scan on `(*f).name.is_null()`, which never fires for the sentinel, so on any spawn key not present in the table (extremely common — e.g. keys like "gametype", editor keys, custom keys, all of which G_SpawnGEntityFromSpawnVars passes to BG_ParseField) the loop runs `f = f.add(1)` past the end of FIELDS and dereferences garbage BG_field_t entries → out-of-bounds read / UB / likely crash. C terminates cleanly because {NULL} yields a null name. The code comment even claims 'name left null' but the code sets a non-null empty-string pointer.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Emit the sentinel with a genuinely null name, e.g. construct it directly as BG_field_t { name: core::ptr::null_mut(), ofs: 0, r#type: fieldtype_t::F_IGNORE, flags: 0 } (or add a null-name variant to the `field` helper). Keep it within g_spawn.rs.

audit_detail.c_quote: trap_SetConfigstring( CS_GAME_VERSION, GAME_VERSION );  /* #define GAME_VERSION "basejka-1" */
audit_detail.rust_quote: GSetConfigstringArgs::new(CS_GAME_VERSION, c"GAME_VERSION".to_owned())
audit_detail.impact: The porter transcribed the macro NAME as a literal string. C expands GAME_VERSION to "basejka-1"; Rust sets configstring CS_GAME_VERSION to the literal text "GAME_VERSION". CS_GAME_VERSION is client/server version-match data — clients would see the wrong version string.

audit_detail.c_quote: angles[1] = fmod(angles[1] + level.mRotationAdjust, 360.0f);
audit_detail.rust_quote: angles[1] = (angles[1] + (*ctx.world).level.mRotationAdjust).rem_euclid(360.0);
audit_detail.impact: rem_euclid is not fmod. For a negative dividend (e.g. angle "-90" plus rotation giving a negative sum) C's fmod returns a negative remainder (sign of dividend) while rem_euclid returns the least non-negative value — they differ by exactly 360 (e.g. C -10 vs Rust 350). The value is then written into the spawn field as "%0.0f". Because these are all rotation angles used mod-360 (ANGLE2SHORT-encoded), the final entity orientation is equivalent, but the stored/parsed intermediate value diverges and a differential test on the raw field/float would flag it. Also fmod is double-precision vs rem_euclid on f32. Three occurrences (angles, angle, direction).
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Replace .rem_euclid(360.0) with a truncated remainder matching fmod, e.g. ((x as f64) % 360.0) as f32 (or f32 `%`), at all three sites.

audit_detail.c_quote: rotation = DEG2RAD(level.mRotationAdjust); newOrigin[0] = origin[0]*cos(rotation) - origin[1]*sin(rotation);
audit_detail.rust_quote: let rotation = (*ctx.world).level.mRotationAdjust.to_radians(); new_origin[0] = origin[0]*rotation.cos() - origin[1]*rotation.sin();
audit_detail.impact: C's cos()/sin() are the double libm functions and origin[k]*cos(...) evaluates in f64 before narrowing to the f32 newOrigin; Rust uses f32 rotation.cos()/sin() so the whole expression is f32. Also to_radians() computes self*(PI/180) whereas DEG2RAD is (a*M_PI)/180.0F — a reassociation that rounds differently. Result is passed through "%0.0f" so the observable impact is a rare rounding flip near .5 boundaries; still a genuine FP-width divergence.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Compute the rotation/cos/sin in f64 to mirror C (e.g. (origin[0] as f64)*(rotation as f64).cos() - …) then narrow to f32, matching the double libm path.

audit_detail.c_quote: *out = atoi( s );
audit_detail.rust_quote: unsafe fn c_str_to_i32(s) -> c_int { c_str_to_f64(s) as c_int }  // c_str_to_f64 accepts '.', 'e','E','+','-'
audit_detail.impact: G_SpawnInt is atoi (stops at first non-digit). The port routes through c_str_to_f64 which accepts '.', 'e'/'E', sign — so e.g. "1e3" yields 1000 (atoi gives 1) and "12.9" yields 12 via float truncation rather than atoi's leading-integer parse. Only diverges for int spawn values containing '.'/'e', which is unusual in map data; low impact but a real helper-semantics divergence.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Implement c_str_to_i32 with true atoi semantics (parse an optional sign then consecutive ASCII digits only), independent of the float parser.

audit_detail.impact: Wrong operand: C guards the hack-start branch with `other->s.number < MAX_CLIENTS` (toucher is a real client); the port uses `self_->s.number` (the trigger). audit_detail.impact: Entire fPartial computation is done in f32 where Raven promotes through f64: VectorLength uses double sqrt (see q_math.rs:249 which casts to f64), `acos` is double libm, and RAD2DEG divides by M_PI (double). audit_detail.c_quote: VectorMA( velocity, -2*dot*bounceFactor, trace->plane.normal, ent->s.pos.trDelta ); ... VectorCopy( tr.endpos, ent->r.currentOrigin );
audit_detail.rust_quote: crate::q_math::_VectorMA(velocity, -2.0f32*dot*bounce_factor, unsafe{(*trace).plane.normal}, &mut unsafe { (*ent).s.pos.trDelta });
audit_detail.impact: `&mut unsafe { PLACE }` parses as `&mut (unsafe{PLACE})`; the unsafe block is a VALUE expression, so it produces a temporary COPY of the vec3_t ([f32;3] is Copy) and `&mut` borrows the temporary. The out-param write lands in the discarded temporary and never reaches the entity field. Verified with rustc: `&mut unsafe{(*p).a}` leaves the field [0,0,0]; `unsafe{&mut (*p).a}` writes correctly. All 22 sites are output args to _VectorCopy/_VectorMA/_VectorScale/BG_EvaluateTrajectory writing gentity fields (trDelta, trBase, currentOrigin, currentAngles, apos.trType-adjacent copies, pos1, s.origin). Consequence: G_BounceObject never stores the reflected velocity or stop-position; G_RunObject never updates currentOrigin from the trace, never updates currentAngles, never applies zero-G friction, never sets apos.trBase; G_StopObjectMoving/G_StartObjectMoving never write s.origin/trBase/trDelta. Object physics is entirely non-functional and diverges from C. HolocronThink (g_misc.rs) dispatches into the broken G_RunObject.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: At every one of the 22 sites, move `&mut` INSIDE the unsafe block so it borrows the place: replace `&mut unsafe { (*ent).s.pos.trDelta }` with `unsafe { &mut (*ent).s.pos.trDelta }`. (Local-target calls like `&mut old_org`/`&mut origin`/`&mut velocity` are already correct.)

audit_detail.c_quote: ent->random = sin( M_PI * ent->random / 180 );
audit_detail.rust_quote: (*ent).random = (std::f32::consts::PI * (*ent).random / 180.0).sin();
audit_detail.impact: C evaluates in double: M_PI is a double, `/180` promotes to double, and sin() is the double libm — the whole expression is computed in f64 then narrowed to the float field. The port uses f32 PI, f32 division, and f32 `.sin()`, computing entirely in f32. audit_detail.proposed_fix: Compute in f64 and narrow: `(*ent).random = (std::f64::consts::PI * (*ent).random as f64 / 180.0).sin() as f32;`

len = strlen( temp );
		if ( (fatalErrorPointer-fatalErrorString)+len >= sizeof( fatalErrorString ) )
audit_detail.rust_quote:
let len = temp.len();
            if (*ctx.world).globals.fatalErrors as usize + len >= 4096 {
audit_detail.impact: The fatalErrorString overflow guard was transcribed with the WRONG state variable: C compares the running BYTE OFFSET written so far (`fatalErrorPointer - fatalErrorString`, modeled in Rust as the usize field `fatalErrorPointer` which is used as the write index at line 2081-2085) plus `len` against 4096; the Rust instead compares `fatalErrors` (the count of errors, incremented by 1 per call at line 2045). Since `fatalErrorPointer` grows by ~`len` (tens of bytes) per error while `fatalErrors` grows by 1, the two diverge quickly. Consequence: the Com_Error(ERR_DROP) abort fires far later than C, and the subsequent write loop `fatalErrorString.0[start + i]` (start = fatalErrorPointer) indexes the fixed 4096-byte array out of bounds and PANICS in Rust before the guard ever trips, whereas C aborts cleanly. This is reachable whenever NAV_CalculatePaths runs on a map with enough >1024-unit waypoint connections to fill the buffer.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Change the guard to use the byte offset: `if (*ctx.world).globals.fatalErrorPointer + len >= 4096 {`. (Separately, the Com_Error message text also drops the C `fatalErrorString`+`fatalErrors` prefix/count, but that is cosmetic within the abort path.)

audit_detail.impact: The line 835 `_VectorCopy(localPlayerMaxs, &mut mins)` is a FAITHFUL transcription of Raven's own bug (C copies playerMaxs into `mins`, not `maxs`). But a side effect of that bug is that in the ignoreEnt==null branch, C leaves local `maxs` UNINITIALIZED, then reads it in `if (mins[2] > maxs[2])` and passes it to trap_Trace (C UB / garbage box). The Rust declares `maxs = [0.0f32; 3]` at line 827, so it deterministically uses a zeroed maxs — a defined-behavior §19 choice for C's UB, but it is undocumented at the site. No in-tree caller currently passes a null ignoreEnt (NAVNEW_MoveToGoal passes self_), so this is latent. Add a ~2-line §19 note documenting the zeroed-maxs choice, or leave as-is if the divergence is accepted.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Add a §19 note at the else-branch (line 833-836) stating that C leaves `maxs` uninitialized here due to the faithfully-preserved double-copy-into-mins bug, and the Rust deterministically uses the zeroed `maxs`. No behavioral change.

audit_detail.impact: The `impactPos` out-param is taken BY VALUE (`vec3_t` = a copied `[f32;3]`), so writing `tr.endpos` into it never reaches the caller's storage. In C `impactPos` is `float*` and the trace endpoint is written back to the caller. Callers read it: NPC_AI_Jedi.rs:801 does `if VectorCompare(impactPos, vec3_origin) != qfalse` right after calling — in C impactPos is filled (non-zero) so this is false and the fallback trace is skipped; in Rust impactPos stays at the caller's cleared vec3_origin so the branch is always taken, running a different fallback trace and diverging the aim/shoot decision. Stormtrooper (impactPos static, read at 1449/1481/1510) and GalakMech (impactPos4, read at 495/516/533) are likewise affected. The PORT-NOTE's reasoning ('caller owns the array … always writes through') is incorrect for a by-value array. Fix: make the param `Option<&mut vec3_t>` (matching the established out-param reshape used by G_GetBoltPosition/CalcEntitySpot) and write through it.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Change signature to `impactPos: Option<&mut vec3_t>` and, on the `if let Some(p) = impactPos` path, `*p = tr.endpos;` (Grenadier passes None for C's NULL). Update the 7 call sites to pass `Some(&mut impactPos)`.

audit_detail.impact: G_CheckForDanger. The Rust factors the C 3-way OR into a `Some/None` split on `owner && owner->client`. The `None` branch is reached exactly when `!owner || !owner->client` — both of which make the C condition TRUE — so it must yield `true`. Instead it yields `owner.is_null()`, which is FALSE for the case owner!=NULL but owner->client==NULL (a non-client alert owner such as a missile/breakable). In that case C flees (enters the danger-flee block, calling NPC_StartFlee / returning qtrue) while Rust does not flee and returns qfalse. Secondary (benign here): the `Some` branch adds a `self->client != null` guard C lacks — harmless because G_CheckForDanger's self is always an NPC with a client.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Change the `else` arm to `true` (reaching it already implies `!owner || !owner->client`).

audit_detail.impact: G_FindLocalInterestPoint. In C `fabs()` returns double, so `fabs(a)+fabs(b)` and the `/2 < 48` / `> |z|` comparisons are evaluated in double; the Rust `.abs()` is f32 and the sum/compare are f32. The single `fabs` values are exact in both, but the *sum of two f32 magnitudes* rounds in f32 whereas it is exact in f64, so at the two decision boundaries (`<48` skip test, and the up/down-look test) the result can flip for positions whose true sum/2 lies within ~1 f32-ULP of the threshold. Boundary-only, low frequency.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Evaluate the magnitude sum in f64 to match C, e.g. `((diff_vec[0].abs() as f64 + diff_vec[1].abs() as f64)/2.0)` for both comparisons.

audit_detail.impact: ClearPlayerAlertEvents (and identically RemoveOldestAlert:955). C's memmove shifts elements [i+1..MAX) down into [i..MAX-1) and leaves the final slot alertEvents[MAX-1] untouched (stale). audit_detail.rust_quote: animations = animations.offset((fallback_anim - anim) as isize);
audit_detail.impact: C's droid fallback reassigns the local `anim = BOTH_WALK2`, so all downstream code (the SETANIM_FLAG_OVERRIDE `!= anim` comparisons, BG_SetAnimFinal, and BG_StartTorsoAnim/BG_StartLegsAnim which do `ps->torsoAnim/legsAnim = anim`) uses BOTH_WALK2. The Rust keeps `anim` at the original value and instead shifts the `animations` pointer by (fallback_anim-anim). This makes the frame DATA (numFrames/frameLerp/firstFrame) correctly read WALK2, but the stored ps->torsoAnim/ps->legsAnim (and the restart/flip comparisons) keep the ORIGINAL anim number (RUN1/WALKBACK1/RUNBACK1) instead of BOTH_WALK2. For droid/NPC models whose animation.cfg lacks RUN1/WALKBACK1/RUNBACK1 frames, the recorded anim number diverges from the oracle, corrupting restart detection (BG_FlipPart), the OVERRIDE timer-clear comparison, and next-frame anim continuation.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Faithfully reassign the anim number rather than shifting the pointer: set `anim = fallback_anim` (make `anim` mutable) after the empty-frame re-check, and index `animations[anim]` directly, so the reassignment propagates to BG_StartTorsoAnim/BG_StartLegsAnim and the OVERRIDE comparisons exactly as in C.

audit_detail.c_quote: float		fps; ... fps = atof( token ); ... animset[animNum].frameLerp = ceil(1000.0f / fps);
audit_detail.rust_quote: let mut fps: f64; ... fps = atof(token); ... (*animset.offset(animNum as isize)).frameLerp = (1000.0 / fps).ceil() as i16;
audit_detail.impact: In C `fps` is a `float` (atof's double result is narrowed to float on assignment) and `1000.0f / fps` is a single-precision float division; floor/ceil then run on that float value. The Rust declares `fps: f64` (atof returns f64, kept at full precision) and evaluates `1000.0 / fps` in f64. Both the operand width (fps f32 vs f64) and the division width (f32 vs f64) diverge from C. For any fps not exactly representable as f32, or where the f32 vs f64 quotient straddles an integer boundary, floor()/ceil() yield a frameLerp differing by 1, changing every anim's frame timing for that entry (frameLerp feeds BG_AnimLength and all HOLD timers).
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Match C's single precision: declare `fps` as f32 (`fps = atof(token) as f32;`) and compute `(1000.0f32 / fps).floor()`/`.ceil()` so the division stays f32.

audit_detail.c_quote: ps->torsoTimer /= 1.7; ... ps->legsTimer /= 1.3; ... ps->legsTimer /= 1.7;
audit_detail.rust_quote: (*ps).torsoTimer = ((*ps).torsoTimer as f32 / 1.7) as c_int;
audit_detail.impact: C's `int /= 1.7` (and /1.3) promotes the int timer to double and divides by the double literal, then truncates back to int. The Rust divides `timer as f32` by an f32 `1.7`/`1.3` literal. Because 1.7f/1.3f differ from 1.7/1.3 in the ~7th digit, the truncated integer can differ by 1 (e.g. timer=17: C 17/1.7=10, Rust 17.0f/1.7f=9.99999->9). Under FP_RAGE (torso and legs) or FP_SPEED (legs) with a HOLD anim, the resulting torsoTimer/legsTimer can be off by one relative to the oracle.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Evaluate the division in f64 to match C: e.g. `(*ps).torsoTimer = ((*ps).torsoTimer as f64 / 1.7) as c_int;` for all three sites (1.7 torso, 1.3 and 1.7 legs).

audit_detail.c_quote: amt = (time - saber->blade[i].extendDebounce)*0.01;
audit_detail.rust_quote: let mut amt = (time - blade.extendDebounce) as f32 * 0.01;
audit_detail.impact: C: `(int - int)` is int, then `* 0.01` promotes the int to double (0.01 is a double literal), the product is computed in f64, then narrowed to the `float amt` on store. Rust: `(...) as f32` makes the left operand f32, so `0.01` is inferred f32 and the whole multiply is done in single precision. Because 0.01 has different f32 vs f64 representations, the narrowed result differs by up to 1 ULP for most inputs. `amt` then drives `blade.length += amt` (and its clamps), so blade length animation can diverge from the oracle by 1 ULP and accumulate.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Match C's f64 evaluation: `let mut amt = ((time - blade.extendDebounce) as f64 * 0.01) as f32;`

audit_detail.impact: C has NO `continue` after the fallback reset: it falls through with the stale empty token, fails the `Q_stricmp(token,useSaber)` check, then runs `SkipBracedSection(&p)` on the freshly-reset buffer (which consumes exactly the first block's name token since depth stays 0). audit_detail.c_quote: z = (sqrt(apexHeight + z) - sqrt(apexHeight));   // and line 832: time = sqrt( height / ( .5 * NPC->client->ps.gravity ) );
audit_detail.rust_quote: z = (apexHeight + z).sqrt() - apexHeight.sqrt();   // and :806  let time = (height / (0.5 * (*npc_client).ps.gravity as f32)).sqrt();
audit_detail.impact: FP-width divergence in NPC_BSJump. C's `sqrt()` is the libm double routine: `apexHeight + z` (f32) is promoted to double, sqrt taken in double, and (at :832) `.5 * gravity` is a double product with the f32 `height` promoted to double before the double sqrt; results are then narrowed to the f32 locals. The Rust ports use f32 `.sqrt()` and f32 `0.5`, evaluating entirely in f32. For non-perfect-square operands the two sqrt paths differ, so the computed apex-parabola `z`, the flight `time`, and the resulting launch velocity diverge from the oracle bit-for-bit.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Evaluate through f64 to match C: e.g. `z = (((apexHeight + z) as f64).sqrt() - (apexHeight as f64).sqrt()) as f32;` and `let time = ((height as f64) / (0.5 * (*npc_client).ps.gravity as f64)).sqrt() as f32;` (note APEX_HEIGHT/MIN_ANGLE_ERROR must also be fixed for this function to match).

audit_detail.impact: C's `fabs(du0)<EPSILON` compares in f64: du0 (f32) promotes exactly to f64, and EPSILON is the unsuffixed double literal 0.000001 (~1.00000000e-6). audit_detail.c_quote: q_shared.h:547-548: `#ifndef M_PI\n#define M_PI 3.14159265358979323846f\n#endif` (note the trailing `f`) and :1174 `#define DEG2RAD(a) (((a)*M_PI)/180.0F)`. The project's own oracle shim documents this explicitly: qshared_shim.h:38 `// from q_shared.h — note the `f` suffix: M_PI is a *float* constant here.` and :56 `// from q_shared.h — all-float angle conversions (NOT OpenJK's precomputed-constant form).`
audit_detail.rust_quote: q_math.rs:492: `let rad = ((degrees as f64 * std::f64::consts::PI) / 180.0) as f32;` — and identically shaped `std::f64::consts::PI`-based conversions in vectoangles/AngleVectors/NormalToLatLong/G_FindClosestPointOnLineSegment/G_PointDistFromLineSegment
audit_detail.impact: This codebase's own q_shared.h overrides the general 'M_PI is a double' assumption (stated in docs/porting-rules.md and repeated in nearly every comment in this file) by redefining M_PI as an `f`-suffixed float literal, and the oracle_c shim used for this repo's actual differential-testing ground truth explicitly preserves that override. Consequently DEG2RAD/RAD2DEG and every raw `angle * M_PI` expression in the oracle evaluate ENTIRELY in float precision using the float-rounded pi value (~3.1415927410125732), not full double pi. The Rust port instead computes these conversions using `std::f64::consts::PI` (true double pi) and often widens the whole expression to f64 before the trig call, the opposite of the oracle's actual float-then-widen-for-libm order. Net effect: RotatePointAroundVector, vectoangles, AngleVectors, NormalToLatLong, G_FindClosestPointOnLineSegment/G_PointDistFromLineSegment (and mirrored sites in bg_misc.rs) produce trig results differing from the oracle in the last few ULPs — small but real, systemic, and exactly what an exact-parity differential test is meant to catch.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Add a `RAVEN_M_PI_F32: f32 = 3.14159265358979323846_f32` constant (matching the oracle's literal) and rewrite each DEG2RAD/RAD2DEG-shaped conversion to first compute the float-only product/quotient exactly as the C macro does (e.g. `degrees * RAVEN_M_PI_F32 / 180.0f32`), only then widening that single f32 result to f64 before calling `.sin()/.cos()/.atan2()` (matching C's implicit float-to-double promotion at the libm call), narrowing the libm result back to f32 for storage.

For any `path` argument longer than 63 characters (a real possibility for deep asset/model paths in Jedi Academy), the port concatenates the extension onto the *full* untruncated path, producing a different (and longer) result string than the oracle.

audit_detail.c_quote: q_shared.c:1309: `Com_sprintf (newi, sizeof(newi), "\\%s\\%s", key, value);` — `newi` is `char newi[MAX_INFO_STRING]` (1024) / `[BIG_INFO_STRING]` (8192); Com_sprintf truncates its output to fit that buffer (with an overflow warning), so `strlen(newi)` in the following length check is bounded by the buffer size.

audit_detail.impact: When `key`+`value` combined would overflow the oracle's `newi[MAX_INFO_STRING]`/`newi[BIG_INFO_STRING]` buffer, the oracle's Com_sprintf silently truncates `newi` to the buffer size (with a printed warning) and the subsequent length check operates on that truncated length — meaning the oracle can still apply a truncated (garbled) update in some cases. audit_detail.c_quote: q_shared.c:489-491: `if (c=='\"' || !c) { com_token[len] = 0; *data_p = (char*)data; return com_token; }` — unlike the word-parsing path below it, this quoted-string path never resets `len` to 0 when `len == MAX_TOKEN_CHARS`, so a quoted token exactly at/over MAX_TOKEN_CHARS writes `com_token[MAX_TOKEN_CHARS]`, one past the array end (C UB — a silent overwrite of adjacent static storage on most compilers).
audit_detail.rust_quote: q_shared.rs:576: `COM_TOKEN[len as usize] = 0;` with `COM_TOKEN: [c_char; 1024]` — reachable with `len == 1024`, which panics (index out of bounds) in Rust instead of silently corrupting memory as in C
audit_detail.impact: This is a faithful transcription of an oracle bug (the same guard the word-parsing path applies is missing here) — behaviorally correct up to the point of divergence, but it is exactly the class of silent-C-UB site porting-rules §19 asks to be diverged from deliberately and documented. Currently there's no such note, and the Rust behavior (panic on a sufficiently long quoted config/map-entity string) is a denial-of-service difference from the oracle's silent memory corruption, worth a documented, deliberate choice rather than an implicit panic.
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Add a §19 note and clamp `len` (or use `len.min(MAX_TOKEN_CHARS - 1)`) before the terminator write in the quoted-string return path, matching the safety the word-parsing path already has.

audit_detail.bugclass: 4 (silent C UB not documented with a §19 note)
audit_detail.c_quote: bg_misc.c:501: `while (i < 128 && powerBuf[i] && powerBuf[i] != '\n' && c < NUM_FORCE_POWERS) { ... final_Powers[c] = atoi(readBuf); c++; i++; }` — `int final_Powers[NUM_FORCE_POWERS]` is an uninitialized stack array; if the loop stops early (embedded '\n'), the remaining `final_Powers[c..]` slots are read later while still holding indeterminate stack garbage (C UB).
audit_detail.rust_quote: bg_misc.rs: `for (c, ch) in powers_field.chars().take(NUM_FORCE_POWERS_USIZE).enumerate() { final_powers[c] = ch.to_digit(10).unwrap_or(0) as c_int; }` over a zero-initialized `final_powers` array — does not stop at an embedded '\n' the way the oracle's loop condition does

audit_detail.proposed_fix: Either note this as an intentional, harmless divergence (zero-fill instead of reading UB stack garbage) per §19, or replicate the early stop at an embedded '\n' character for closer positional fidelity.

audit_detail.impact: `0.2` in C is an unsuffixed (double) literal; by the usual arithmetic conversions, `trace->plane.normal[2]` (float) is promoted to double and compared against double `0.2` (≈0.2000000000000000111). Concretely, when `tr.plane.normal[2]` is exactly the float32 value nearest 0.2 (plausible for a hand-authored ramp/slope normal), C's double comparison evaluates `0.20000000298023224 > 0.2` -> true (bounce-stop branch taken: G_SetOrigin + early return), while Rust's float32 comparison evaluates `X > 0.2f32` with X == 0.2f32 -> false (branch skipped, falls through to sound/impact code below). Genuine FP-width divergence per bug class 2 (unsuffixed C literal mixed with a float operand evaluates in double).
audit_detail.proposed_fix: Compare in double precision to match C's promotion: `if (tr.plane.normal[2] as f64) > 0.2 && (crate::q_math::VectorLength((*ent).s.pos.trDelta) as f64) < 40.0`. (Checked the sibling comparison two lines above, `trace->plane.normal[2] > 0.7` at oracle line 166 — it does NOT diverge, because 0.7 rounds DOWN to f32 so the float and double thresholds fall in the same inter-grid-point gap; only the 0.2 case flips.)
